description: Supply chain attack exploiting a prompt injection vulnerability in Cline's AI-powered GitHub issue triage workflow. A malicious actor injected commands via a GitHub issue title, hijacking Cline's CI/CD pipeline, poisoning the Actions cache, stealing npm credentials, and publishing an unauthorized Cline CLI 2.3.0 package that installed OpenClaw on ~4,000 developer machines over an 8-hour window.
agents: Cline's Claude-powered GitHub issue triager (automated, no human-in-the-loop)
The triager read GitHub issue titles as instructions — zero permission gating before execution
Executed CI/CD pipeline commands, cache manipulation, npm publishes without any authorization receipt or approval gate

funding.notes: Cline is an open-source AI coding assistant (VSCode extension, 5M users). This is an incident signal, not a company lead.

contacts.name: Adnan Khan
contacts.title: Security Researcher (discoverer)
contacts.notes: Security researcher who discovered and disclosed the vulnerability. Published at adnanthekhan.com. Potential amplifier contact.

pp_fit.feature: Pre-execution authorization gates with receipts — PP would have stopped the attack at the tool call layer
pp_fit.attack_anatomy: Prompt injection via issue title → AI agent executes malicious commands → no permission gate checked → cache poisoned → npm token stolen → unauthorized package published → 4,000 machines compromised. PP's action-time authorization receipt would have required explicit human approval BEFORE the pipeline trigger and npm publish.
pp_fit.narrative_value: Clinejection is the clearest recent proof that LLM-powered agents executing real-world actions (CI/CD, package publishes) without pre-execution permission gates are supply chain attack vectors. PP is exactly the architectural layer that was missing. Cite in: Twitter threads, blog posts, investor conversations, enterprise sales calls.

incident_timeline.vector: Prompt injection in GitHub issue title → AI triager executes malicious instructions

notes: This is not an outreach target — it's a narrative amplifier. Use in PP content: 'Clinejection happened because there was no PP-style authorization gate before execution. This is what we prevent.' Excellent case study for the PP thesis. Also note: Snyk covered this extensively — Snyk partnership/content angle worth exploring.
